laws.rule: You must always carry proof of identity. Carry a photocopy of your passport with some original identification, such as your driver's licence or another government-issued identity document. Don't drink and drive, penalties are severe for driving with a blood-alcohol level reading over 0%.

laws.rule: You can drive in Brazil for up to 180 days after your arrival, as long as you carry a valid Australian driver’s licence. It is also recommended that you carry a translation of your licence. After this period, you will need to obtain a local driver’s licence.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Brazilian Real (BRL). Declare amounts over USD 10,000 (or foreign currency equivalent) when you arrive and depart. This includes all forms of currency, not just cash. US dollars are the easiest to exchange. Credit cards are widely accepted. Ask your bank in Australia if your ATM card will work and if it has an affiliate bank in Brazil, as some local machines may be unreliable. To combat fraud and theft, many ATMs may limit the amount you can withdraw per day. Credit card fraud is widespread. Take care when making online payments. Check the amount before making payment

layers.authority: Fundação Nacional dos Povos Indígenas (FUNAI), Presidency
layers.process: Entry to an Indigenous land (terra indígena) for research and similar purposes needs written authorisation from the FUNAI Presidency, after prior consent from the representatives of the Indigenous peoples concerned. Apply at least 90 days before entry. Foreign researchers also need a passport copy, visa and an authorisation from the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation; every entrant needs a medical certificate and a yellow fever vaccination record. Use of Indigenous images, sound and works (filming, photography) and journalism follow their own FUNAI rules. The service is free. Tourist visits to Indigenous lands run only under visitation arrangements led by the community; ask FUNAI (aaep@funai.gov.br is the published contact for entry requests) or the community's own association.

layers.authority: FUNAI regional coordination; the Indigenous people or community that proposes the visit
layers.process: Tourism in a terra indígena runs only through a Plano de Visitação (visitation plan) put forward by the Indigenous people, community or their organisation to the FUNAI regional office, under Instrução Normativa 3/2015. If every FUNAI body approves without comment, the FUNAI President issues a Carta de Anuência (letter of consent); the service is free and takes 60 to 90 days. The plan sets group size, visit length, visitor conduct rules and keeping alcohol and drugs out. Visitors carry photo ID and the individual entry authorisation the proposer issues. A tourism authorisation does not replace separate ones for research, religious, commercial or journalistic work. Where the land overlaps a federal conservation unit, FUNAI and ICMBio approve jointly. Whether a community agrees is its own decision; ask the community or FUNAI (cgetno@funai.gov.br).

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: Drones over 250 g are registered in ANAC's SISANT, then flights are requested from DECEA through SARPAS; ANATEL approval of the equipment is also needed. ANAC says foreign drones may enter Brazilian airspace only with ANAC's explicit authorisation. No public operator list found.

items.text: Not yet checked: no public ANAC directory of drone operators was found on the pages read.

SISANT registration is free and declaratory and is mandatory above 250 g, recreational or not. DECEA's SARPAS flight requests need aircraft registered in SISANT. The operator also needs ANATEL homologation and DECEA authorisation or notification to use the airspace.

ANAC's FAQ says foreign unmanned aircraft may cross the border into Brazilian airspace only after ANAC's explicit authorisation and compliance with DECEA rules, and that ANAC does not issue import authorisations (Receita Federal and customs decide). A foreign operator's SISANT or SARPAS route was not found on the pages read.

Open to tourism agencies, tour operators and the press, national or international; free; estimated 1 to 5 business days; download link lasts 7 days. The page does not mention aerial footage.
